provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The native rule samples the input at every second row and column, starting from index 0, so a 6x6 grid becomes 3x3. Under a D4 transform, each lattice axis is either preserved or reversed. A reversed axis puts the lattice on indices 5,3,1 instead of 0,2,4. The factory applies the d4 transform to a 6x6 marker of the original even/even lattice. It then reads off whether the occupied rows and columns now start at index 1, which means the axis is anchored at the far end. The emitted program slices the visible grid directly with stride 2 from the correct start offset on each axis. A far-end-anchored axis starts at (size-1)%2. The scan order is unchanged, so the output orientation matches the transformed output. Colours are copied verbatim, so the palette needs no remapping, and the background (palette[0]) is never consulted.
draft_notes.limitations: The constructor only produces 6x6 inputs and 3x3 outputs, and the offsets are specialized from d4. For other sizes the program extends the convention by anchoring each lattice axis at index 0 or at the far end. The fixtures are consistent with a uniform rule. I have not run any tests.
